product.amstrad-integra-powerpro.summary: The top Integra, with MPEG as standard for Video CD playback.
product.amstrad-integra-powerpro.history: Personal Computer World reviewed the PowerPro 90 in March 1996 at £1,599. Amstrad Direct identified the P100 as its successor and advertised it at £1,299 plus VAT for the British home market.
product.amstrad-integra-powerpro.technic: Integravision let users watch television in a window and capture still frames. The reviewed P90 used a Cirrus Logic GD5434 and a 520 MB drive. The P100 brochure specifies 540 MB.
The configuration has been checked against contemporary sources. The BluMach sheet is in research.
An attributable system BIOS, motherboard identification and validation of boot, TV tuner and remote control remain pending.
The recovery package restores multimedia functions in Windows 95. The preserved Integra Pentium package contains TV and MPEG software.
